info.title: VideoFetch API
info.description:
VideoFetch is a video ingestion API. Send a video URL plus a format and we deliver the MP4/MP3 — optionally trimmed to an exact window — to your own object storage or to a platform delivery link.

Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer vf_live_sk_...` (API key) or a signed-in dashboard session token for account-management endpoints.

Typical flow:
  1. POST /v1/downloads            → 202 { id: "dl_xxxxxxxxxx", status: "queued" }
  2. GET  /v1/downloads/{id}       → poll until completed | failed
  3. Receive download.completed on your webhook, if you registered one

Failed jobs are never charged, and every attempt is recorded on the job. Full guides: https://vidfetch.dev (Documentation).

post.description: Retry delivery of a job that failed at the delivery stage. While the file is held (24h, see `delivery.hold_expires_at`) it is uploaded again without re-downloading the source and without charging again. Omit `destination` to retry the original target (e.g. after fixing permissions), or pass a new one — same forms as `POST /v1/downloads`. Returns 409 `not_redeliverable` when the job did not fail at delivery or the hold has expired.
Create an API key for the signed-in account. Usage draws on the account plan quota.

get.description: Account-level quota snapshot (identical to the dashboard overview), alert state and concurrency headroom.
Live alert state plus the alerts already fired this month (each threshold fires once per month per account).

post.description: Connection test: connect, write a small probe object, then delete it — write permission is verified, not assumed. A malformed config (bucket name, endpoint, region, blocked host) is rejected with 422; a problem found while talking to the bucket returns 200 with `ok: false`, a `storage_*` code, a hint and per-step results. Only PutObject is required; a failed cleanup is reported as a warning.

get.description:
Recent deliveries for one endpoint, plus delivery-health summary.

Delivery semantics: **at-least-once** — the same event id can arrive more than once, so
de-duplicate with the `X-VideoFetch-Delivery` header. Ordering is **not** guaranteed;
sort by `seq` and/or `created_at` if you need a stable order.

post.description:
Re-queue one recorded delivery so it is attempted again.

Useful after fixing your endpoint: a manual replay does not consume the automatic
retry budget.
Send a ping event so you can confirm your endpoint is reachable and your signature verification works.

DeliveryOut.title: DeliveryOut
DeliveryOut.description: Where the file went. `type=url`: platform bucket + `download_url`; `type=storage`: your bucket.

DestinationSpec.title: DestinationSpec
DestinationSpec.description:
Delivery target for the finished file.

- `"st_…"` or `{"id": "st_…"}` — a saved storage connection (Dashboard → Storage, or
  `POST /v1/storage`). Credentials, bucket and provider come from the connection; `type`
  is ignored. `path` / `key` may override the object location for this job only.
- `{"type": "s3"|"r2"|"gcs"|"s3_compatible", "bucket", "access_key_id",
  "secret_access_key", ...}` — inline credentials. They are used for this job only and
  discarded afterwards; pass `"save": true` to keep them as a connection (the response
  then carries its `destination_id`, reuse it on later jobs).
- `"url"` or `{"type": "url"}` — the platform keeps the file and returns a presigned
  `download_url`, even when the account has a default storage connection.
- omitted — the account's default storage connection if one is set, otherwise `url`.

`path` is an object key prefix template, `key` a full object key template.
Variables: `{video_id}` `{job_id}` `{date}` `{format}` (and `{ext}` in `key`).
